newsitem.title: FRANCE: Right's lead eroded in French election race.
newsitem.headline: Right's lead eroded in French election race.

text.p: The French left is gnawing at the lead of the ruling centre-right according to Saturday's opinion polls, the last that can be published before elections on May 25-June 1.

The last four surveys released ahead of the midnight (2200 GMT) ban on publishing polls in the week before the vote all showed Prime Minister Alain Juppe's RPR-UDF coalition slipping slightly but retaining a majority in the National Assembly.
The surveys showed Juppe's conservatives polling less votes that the combined left, but winning more seats because of the single constituency voting system.
Most surveys showed the far-right National Front could win a tiny foothold in parliament and indicated that about a third of voters were still undecided.

A BVA poll gave the conservatives a majority of 50 seats over the combined left, down from 52 a week earlier. It said they would win 302 seats to the combined left's 252 -- 228 for the Socialists, two for their ecologist allies and 22 for the Communists.
A second CSA poll in 24 hours gave the conservatives 297 seats, a 39-seat majority, down from 43.

A Sofres poll forecast a larger, though also reduced majority for the conservatives of between 316 and 341 seats, down from 338-370 a week earlier. It forecast 214-237 seats for the combined left, up from 183-213.
An Ifop poll gave the conservatives 305-345 seats, down from 328-358, with the left up from 177-207 to 210-248.
Sofres and Ifop gave the National Front 0-3 seats. BVA saw it winning one seat and CSA said it would fail to win any.
A 1993 landslide gave the ruling coalition 470 seats in the outgoing assembly to 63 for the Socialists and 22 for the Communists. The National Front had none.

Turning to vote percentages in the election's first round, both Ifop and Sofres saw the allied left polling 46 percent with the centre-right taking around 40 percent and the National Front 13 or 14 percent.

BVA saw the RPR-UDF and allies polling 38.5 percent, up one point. The combined left, including ecologists, was seen polling 46.5 percent, down from 48 percent, with Socialists unchanged at 25 percent and Communists losing one point at 10.5 percent.
The National Front was losing half a point at 14 percent.
CSA saw the RPR-UDF polling 37.5 percent, down from 38, with the Socialists also down half a point at 26.5 percent. Communists were unchanged at 20.5 percent, like the National Front, on 14 percent.
The polls looked only at the 555 constituencies in mainland France and did not cover a further 22 overseas seats, most of which are currently held by the government.
The BVA poll relied on interviews with 2,036 registered voters and was conducted on Thursday and Friday. The CSA poll of 1,012 voters was carried out Friday-Saturday.
The Friday-Saturday Sofres pll covered 1,000 voters and Ifop's Friday survey covered 1,003.
